newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT-C-C Amatil/San Miguel soft drink merger.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-C-C Amatil/San Miguel soft drink merger.

text.p: Australian-based Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd announced on Thursday it had agreed to merge with Coca Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc, which is 70 percent owned by San Miguel Corp.
The following is the Coca-Cola's statement on the A$3.4 merger plan.
"Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd (CCA) announced today that San Miguel Corporation of the Philippines has agreed in principle to combine its soft drinks operations with those of CCA.
"Under the proposal, a San Miguel subsidiary, Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc (CCBPI), will combine with CCA to create the largest Coca-Cola bottling group outside the United States.

"CCBPI which is owned 70 percent by San Miguel and 30 percent by The Coca-Cola Company, is the Philippines' leading soft drinks company. It owns and operates 21 plants throughout the country. It has a 75 percent share of sales, and in 1996 sold 334 million unit cases (1.9 billion litres) of Coca-Cola Company products generating sales of A$1.2 billion (US$911 million) and a net profit of A$144 million (US$112 million).
"CCA is a Coca-Cola anchor bottler currently with operations in 17 countries in Australasia, Asia and Europe, serving 380 million consumers.

"It owns and operates 43 plants and sold 760 million cases of Coca-Cola Company products in 1996 generating sales of A$3.7 billion (US$2.9 billion) and a net profit of A$142 million (US$111 million). It holds soft drink leadership in each of the countries in which it operates.

"Speaking in Sydney, Dean Wills, chairman of CCA said: "This is a major development for CCA and brings together two of the largest Coca-Cola bottling companies, both with a great deal to contribute to the other.
"Our prime long-term objective is to enhance the value of CCA to its shareholders by profitably managing growth both organically and by expansion.
"This transaction helps us accomplish this objective as CCBPI will add immediately and substantially to CCA's earnings and growth prospects.'

"Under the terms of the proposed transaction, CCA will issue 293 million ordinary shares worth approximately A$3.4 billion (US$2.7 billion), based on an average of CCA's share price for the month of March.
"The newly- issued shares will rank for the final dividend to be declared by CCA for the 1997 year.

"Commenting on the proposal, Andres Soriano III, chairman and chief executive officer of San Miguel said: 'The move offers San Miguel a magnificent opportunity to advance its internationalisation program.

"In one dynamic step, we are able to expand the horizon of our soft drinks business from the Philippine domestic market to the international arena through an anchor bottler spanning three continents.'

"Upon completion of the transaction, San Miguel will hold 25 percent of CCA's shares, and will be the second largest shareholder in CCA after The Coca-Cola Company, whose shareholding will be 33 percent.

"'The coming together of these two prominent companies marks the beginning of a new era for the Coca-Cola business in Asia,' said Roberto C. Goizueta, chairman and chief executive officer of The Coca-Cola Company.

"'The combined strength and expertise of both parties will create one of the world's most powerful bottling systems - and, as plans for future expansion unfold, a system capable of building on the tremendous opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region.'
"San Miguel is the Philippines' largest beverage, food and packaging company. It is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange and reported sales in 1996 of P85 billion (A$4.2 billion).
"The transaction is subject to approval by CCA shareholders as well as regulatory authorities including the Australian Foreign Investment Review Board."
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
